[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
James Glasgow Armstrong was reported born in Belfast in 1836. The Hitchcock family genealogy, p. 95, identifies him as the husband of Alma Emily Hitchcock, daughter of Almon Hitchcock and Ruth Emily Barber. It places their marriage at Sidney, Ohio, without giving its date.<ref>[https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/15/The_genealogy_of_the_Hitchcock_family%2C_who_are_descended_from_Matthias_Hitchcock_of_East_Haven%2C_Conn.%2C_and_Luke_Hitchcock_of_Wethersfield%2C_Conn_%28IA_cu31924012053785%29.pdf The genealogy of the Hitchcock family, printed p. 95, Almon Hitchcock family, daughter Alma Emily]. Searchable text inspected; page image uninspected.</ref>
He was a minister at St Louis and later an Episcopalian rector at Monumental Church, Richmond, Virginia. The same genealogy names two daughters: Miriam Marcella, born 10 April 1865 at St Louis, and Agnes Ruth, born 14 July 1872 at Sidney and died 15 June 1873 at Hannibal, Missouri.<ref>Hitchcock genealogy, p. 95, cited above.</ref>
On 24 April 1870 James McClure Glasgow called the St Louis minister his nephew. The missionary’s held 1861 journal also refers to Rev. J. Glasgow Armstrong as his nephew seeking guidance in ministerial studies.<ref>[https://presbyterianhistoryireland.com/publications/heritage/ John Faris, “A Black Sheep,” Heritage, Autumn 2023, quoting the diary entry of 24 April 1870]; [https://revjamesmcclureglasgow.blogspot.com/ James McClure Glasgow journal, p. 82, early 1861 entry]. Published transcriptions; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>
The Heritage article reports Armstrong’s death in 1891, following the St Louis Post obituary of March 1891. An exact death day is not established here.<ref>Faris, “A Black Sheep,” cited above. The obituary itself was not inspected.</ref>
== Research Notes ==
'''Probable mother, 72% subjective confidence:''' [[Glasgow-1779|Jane Glasgow Armstrong]], the missionary’s documented sister. The known married surname, explicit nephew relationship and generation favour this placement, but neither source names Armstrong’s parents. His father remains unknown.

A separate 1838 Antrim Assizes report names Anne Armstrong, wife of John, and her mother Jane Glasgow. It does not give Anne’s birth surname or identify her with the missionary’s sister. Retain this alternative family route; do not merge Anne and Jane or infer John Armstrong as this minister’s father.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050122635/ Freeman’s Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 27 July 1838, p. 3, Antrim Assizes]. Held record reading, not newly inspected.</ref>
No checked existing WikiTree profile was found in the local catalogue and focused public searches for the full name and Hitchcock spouse. Same-name Canadian Armstrongs born in 1889 and 1931 are later men. This is a distinct documentary identity; no live profile creation or merge has occurred. Seek a Belfast baptism, family marriage or contemporary biographical parent statement to test the mother.
